pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes that workflow emails are still sent for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. The fix of PR #6991 was wrong and didn't work as expected. 

The SendGrid endpoint `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/${referenceId}` was not used correctly. This endpoint deletes a cancelled scheduled email from `scheduled_sends` by removing the 'cancel' status (so email will again be scheduled). 

The reason why cancelling our scheduled emails stopped working is that all cancerlled emails are saved in `scheduled_sends` until the scheduled date but the max. of pending cancellations is 100. Once we reached 100 pending cancellations, new cancellations failed and emails were still sent out. 

The solution implemented in this PR: 
- A new field `cancelled` is added to the `workflowReminder` model
- Once an already scheduled email is cancelled, the field is set to true (nothing else is done at this point in time)
- The CRON job `scheduleEmailReminders` is responsible for the final cancellation of the scheduled email (runs every 15 mins)
  - cancels all scheduled emails that are cancelled and that have their scheduled date within the next hour

Fixes #7225

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Chore (refactoring code, technical debt, workflow improvements)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update
pr.title: Fixes that workflow reminders of cancelled and rescheduled bookings are still sent

raw_findings.body: Only the database flag is updated, so SendGrid reaches the original send time first and delivers a workflow email for the cancelled booking.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The provider sends an imminent reminder before the cancellation worker observes the flag.
raw_findings.impact: Only the database flag is updated, so SendGrid reaches the original send time first and delivers a workflow email for the cancelled booking.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch replaces immediate provider cancellation with a flag that is serviced by a periodic worker without accounting for the worker's maximum latency.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the scheduled date into this operation and cancel synchronously when the reminder is due within at least one cron interval plus a safety margin; defer only reminders that are guaranteed to be processed before send time.
raw_findings.title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders due before the next cron run
raw_findings.trigger: A booking is cancelled just after the 15-minute cron has run, and one of its scheduled emails is due before the next cron invocation.

raw_findings.body: The `true` argument immediately places the batch in SendGrid's cancellation queue until its future send date, continuing to consume one of the 100 pending-cancellation slots that this patch is intended to preserve. Enough reschedules can therefore make later cancellations fail and allow stale emails to be sent.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Far-future reschedules exhaust the provider's pending-cancellation quota.
raw_findings.impact: The `true` argument immediately places the batch in SendGrid's cancellation queue until its future send date, continuing to consume one of the 100 pending-cancellation slots that this patch is intended to preserve. Enough reschedules can therefore make later cancellations fail and allow stale emails to be sent.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new reschedule path explicitly bypasses the just-in-time cancellation mechanism.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the immediate flag on this reschedule path and persist `cancelled: true`, allowing the cron worker to cancel the email shortly before its scheduled date.
raw_findings.title: Rescheduling still creates long-lived SendGrid cancellations
raw_findings.trigger: A booking with a scheduled email more than an hour in the future is rescheduled through handleNewBooking.

raw_findings.body: The cron attempts to place all of them in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue, so requests after the provider's 100-item limit fail and those emails remain scheduled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A valid high-volume cancellation batch exceeds the provider quota that motivated the change.
raw_findings.impact: The cron attempts to place all of them in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue, so requests after the provider's 100-item limit fail and those emails remain scheduled.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fixed one-hour horizon bounds cancellation duration but does not bound the number of pending cancellations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not submit reminders to SendGrid so far in advance that more cancellations can be pending than the provider permits, or implement a capacity-aware, shorter scheduling/cancellation window with retries guaranteed before each send time.
raw_findings.title: A one-hour cancellation batch can itself exceed SendGrid's 100-item limit
raw_findings.trigger: More than 100 cancelled reminders have send times within the same upcoming hour.

raw_findings.body: The enclosing catch exits the loop, skips every later reminder, and also skips deletion of all records whose provider cancellations had already succeeded. Later uncancelled reminders may reach their send times.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single provider error blocks unrelated cancellation work and cleanup.
raw_findings.impact: The enclosing catch exits the loop, skips every later reminder, and also skips deletion of all records whose provider cancellations had already succeeded. Later uncancelled reminders may reach their send times.
raw_findings.root_cause: The whole cancellation loop and its deferred cleanup are enclosed in a single fail-fast try/catch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Catch errors per reminder, continue processing subsequent rows, and delete each successfully cancelled database row immediately rather than deferring all deletes until after the loop.
raw_findings.title: One invalid reminder aborts cancellation of the entire cron batch
raw_findings.trigger: SendGrid rejects one reminder in `remindersToCancel`, for example because its reference ID is stale, while later reminders in the result still require cancellation.

raw_findings.body: The booking is reported as cancelled even though its reminder may never be marked or removed, allowing the old email or SMS to be delivered.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reminder cancellation runs as untracked background work outside the request lifecycle.
raw_findings.impact: The booking is reported as cancelled even though its reminder may never be marked or removed, allowing the old email or SMS to be delivered.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removes the previously awaited reminder-deletion promises but invokes the replacement async helpers without awaiting their returned promises.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the changed `forEach` calls with promise-producing `map`/`flatMap` operations and await `Promise.all` before completing the mutation or deleting parent records.
raw_findings.title: Cancellation promises are discarded across the changed call sites
raw_findings.trigger: A cancellation handler or another changed `forEach` call site completes its response before the asynchronous reminder update/delete finishes, particularly in a serverless process that is frozen after the response.

raw_findings.body: The helper's catch logs and resolves successfully, so callers cannot fail or retry the cancellation and the still-active SendGrid reminder is eventually sent.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A failed state transition is indistinguishable from a successful cancellation.
raw_findings.impact: The helper's catch logs and resolves successfully, so callers cannot fail or retry the cancellation and the still-active SendGrid reminder is eventually sent.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new durable cancellation-state update was placed inside a best-effort helper that suppresses every exception.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Let the update error propagate after logging, and have awaited callers retry or return a failure instead of treating cancellation as successful.
raw_findings.title: Persistence failures are swallowed while marking an email cancelled
raw_findings.trigger: The Prisma update fails because of a transient database error, connection failure, or concurrent deletion.

raw_findings.body: Active reminders are stored and exposed as `NULL` rather than `false`, so boolean filters such as `cancelled: false` omit them and every consumer must account for an undocumented third state.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Database state no longer has an unambiguous true/false representation of cancellation.
raw_findings.impact: Active reminders are stored and exposed as `NULL` rather than `false`, so boolean filters such as `cancelled: false` omit them and every consumer must account for an undocumented third state.
raw_findings.root_cause: A binary status field was introduced as nullable without a default.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Define the field as `Boolean @default(false)` and make the migration add a non-null column with a false default or backfill existing rows before applying `NOT NULL`.
raw_findings.title: The cancellation flag unnecessarily permits a third null state
raw_findings.trigger: Any existing reminder or any newly created reminder that does not explicitly provide `cancelled`.

raw_findings.body: The new `cancelled = true` plus scheduled-date lookup must repeatedly scan the table, increasing cron latency and making time-sensitive cancellations more likely to miss their send times.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation work slows as reminder volume grows rather than scaling with the small set of cancelled rows.
raw_findings.impact: The new `cancelled = true` plus scheduled-date lookup must repeatedly scan the table, increasing cron latency and making time-sensitive cancellations more likely to miss their send times.
raw_findings.root_cause: The migration adds a field used by a frequent time-bounded worker query without adding a corresponding index.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an index supporting the worker query, preferably a partial index on `scheduledDate` for rows where `cancelled = true` and the method is email.
raw_findings.title: The new cron lookup has no supporting cancellation index
raw_findings.trigger: The WorkflowReminder table contains a large number of future reminders while the email cron executes every 15 minutes.

validated_findings.failure_mode: A valid high-volume cancellation batch exceeds the provider quota that motivated the change.
validated_findings.impact: The cron attempts to place all of them in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue, so requests after the provider's 100-item limit fail and those emails remain scheduled.
validated_findings.root_cause: The fixed one-hour horizon bounds cancellation duration but does not bound the number of pending cancellations.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Do not submit reminders to SendGrid so far in advance that more cancellations can be pending than the provider permits, or implement a capacity-aware, shorter scheduling/cancellation window with retries guaranteed before each send time.
validated_findings.title: A one-hour cancellation batch can itself exceed SendGrid's 100-item limit
validated_findings.trigger: More than 100 cancelled reminders have send times within the same upcoming hour.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that >100 cancelled reminders in one hour will exceed SendGrid's limit is speculative. The patch does not introduce unbounded batching; the 1-hour window bounds duration, not count, but there is no evidence the system routinely has >100 cancellations per hour or that this is a new defect introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The enclosing catch exits the loop, skips every later reminder, and also skips deletion of all records whose provider cancellations had already succeeded. Later uncancelled reminders may reach their send times.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A single provider error blocks unrelated cancellation work and cleanup.
validated_findings.impact: The enclosing catch exits the loop, skips every later reminder, and also skips deletion of all records whose provider cancellations had already succeeded. Later uncancelled reminders may reach their send times.
validated_findings.root_cause: The whole cancellation loop and its deferred cleanup are enclosed in a single fail-fast try/catch.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Catch errors per reminder, continue processing subsequent rows, and delete each successfully cancelled database row immediately rather than deferring all deletes until after the loop.
validated_findings.title: One invalid reminder aborts cancellation of the entire cron batch
validated_findings.trigger: SendGrid rejects one reminder in `remindersToCancel`, for example because its reference ID is stale, while later reminders in the result still require cancellation.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 53-77 show a single try/catch wrapping the entire for-loop and subsequent Promise.all. If any SendGrid request fails, the catch at L75 logs and exits, skipping remaining cancellations and all pending deletes. This is a fail-fast pattern introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The booking is reported as cancelled even though its reminder may never be marked or removed, allowing the old email or SMS to be delivered.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Reminder cancellation runs as untracked background work outside the request lifecycle.
validated_findings.impact: The booking is reported as cancelled even though its reminder may never be marked or removed, allowing the old email or SMS to be delivered.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch removes the previously awaited reminder-deletion promises but invokes the replacement async helpers without awaiting their returned promises.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the changed `forEach` calls with promise-producing `map`/`flatMap` operations and await `Promise.all` before completing the mutation or deleting parent records.
validated_findings.title: Cancellation promises are discarded across the changed call sites
validated_findings.trigger: A cancellation handler or another changed `forEach` call site completes its response before the asynchronous reminder update/delete finishes, particularly in a serverless process that is frozen after the response.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch at L485-492 shows `forEach` calling async helpers without await. In serverless environments, the response can complete before these fire-and-forget promises finish, leaving reminders uncancelled. The old code awaited `remindersToDelete` via `Promise.all`.

validated_findings.body: The helper's catch logs and resolves successfully, so callers cannot fail or retry the cancellation and the still-active SendGrid reminder is eventually sent.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A failed state transition is indistinguishable from a successful cancellation.
validated_findings.impact: The helper's catch logs and resolves successfully, so callers cannot fail or retry the cancellation and the still-active SendGrid reminder is eventually sent.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new durable cancellation-state update was placed inside a best-effort helper that suppresses every exception.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Let the update error propagate after logging, and have awaited callers retry or return a failure instead of treating cancellation as successful.
validated_findings.title: Persistence failures are swallowed while marking an email cancelled
validated_findings.trigger: The Prisma update fails because of a transient database error, connection failure, or concurrent deletion.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The catch block at L233-235 logs and continues, but the claim that this swallows the Prisma update error is incorrect for the deferred path. The update is inside the try block; if it throws, the catch logs it. However, the function does not re-throw, so callers cannot detect failure. This is a valid concern but the candidate conflates the immediate-delete path (which returns early) with the deferred path. The impact is overstated since the deferred path is the only one reaching L225.

validated_findings.body: Active reminders are stored and exposed as `NULL` rather than `false`, so boolean filters such as `cancelled: false` omit them and every consumer must account for an undocumented third state.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Database state no longer has an unambiguous true/false representation of cancellation.
validated_findings.impact: Active reminders are stored and exposed as `NULL` rather than `false`, so boolean filters such as `cancelled: false` omit them and every consumer must account for an undocumented third state.
validated_findings.root_cause: A binary status field was introduced as nullable without a default.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Define the field as `Boolean @default(false)` and make the migration add a non-null column with a false default or backfill existing rows before applying `NOT NULL`.
validated_findings.title: The cancellation flag unnecessarily permits a third null state
validated_findings.trigger: Any existing reminder or any newly created reminder that does not explicitly provide `cancelled`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Schema at L644 shows `cancelled Boolean?` with no default. Existing rows and new rows without explicit `cancelled` will have NULL, requiring queries to use `cancelled: true` or `cancelled IS NOT DISTINCT FROM false` rather than `cancelled: false`.

validated_findings.body: The new `cancelled = true` plus scheduled-date lookup must repeatedly scan the table, increasing cron latency and making time-sensitive cancellations more likely to miss their send times.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation work slows as reminder volume grows rather than scaling with the small set of cancelled rows.
validated_findings.impact: The new `cancelled = true` plus scheduled-date lookup must repeatedly scan the table, increasing cron latency and making time-sensitive cancellations more likely to miss their send times.
validated_findings.root_cause: The migration adds a field used by a frequent time-bounded worker query without adding a corresponding index.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add an index supporting the worker query, preferably a partial index on `scheduledDate` for rows where `cancelled = true` and the method is email.
validated_findings.title: The new cron lookup has no supporting cancellation index
validated_findings.trigger: The WorkflowReminder table contains a large number of future reminders while the email cron executes every 15 minutes.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing index is a performance concern, not a correctness bug. The patch adds a column; whether an index is needed depends on table size and query patterns. This is speculative and stylistic rather than a concrete defect introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: Symbols used only as types are treated as runtime dependencies, violating the file's prior type-import convention and potentially causing lint failures or invalid ESM imports for type-only Prisma exports.
validated_findings.evidence:
import {
  App,
  BookingStatus,
  Credential,
  EventTypeCustomInput,
  Prisma,
validated_findings.failure_mode: Static checks fail or emitted module dependencies no longer accurately represent runtime usage.
validated_findings.impact: Symbols used only as types are treated as runtime dependencies, violating the file's prior type-import convention and potentially causing lint failures or invalid ESM imports for type-only Prisma exports.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch merged an existing type-only import into the runtime Prisma import merely to add an enum value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore `import type { App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma }` and keep only runtime values such as `BookingStatus` and `WorkflowMethods` in the normal import; apply the same correction to the changed workflows router imports.
validated_findings.title: Prisma model types were converted to value imports
validated_findings.trigger: Type-aware linting or a TypeScript configuration that preserves value imports processes this module.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The import change at L1-10 consolidates type and value imports. TypeScript's `isolatedModules` or `verbatimModuleSyntax` would flag this if problematic, but the repository does not show such config. This is a stylistic concern, not a bug introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The missing trailing comma and associated patch-wide de-indentation create formatter churn and can fail a format-checking CI job.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Formatting validation or review quality is degraded by avoidable, unrelated whitespace changes.
validated_findings.impact: The missing trailing comma and associated patch-wide de-indentation create formatter churn and can fail a format-checking CI job.
validated_findings.root_cause: The import consolidation and surrounding whitespace edits were committed without applying the repository's multiline formatting convention.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Run the repository formatter on the file and revert the unrelated indentation-only changes in the commented block.
validated_findings.title: The workflows router import is left unformatted
validated_findings.trigger: The repository formatter or formatting check processes the changed router.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing trailing comma and formatting is purely stylistic. The patch shows valid TypeScript syntax at L9. Formatting churn is not a functional defect.
